summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of chronic alcohol use, COPD, atrial fibrillation, and prior strokes was admitted with fever, cough, and chest pain concerning for pneumonia. Community-acquired pneumonia was treated with antibiotics, and imaging confirmed left lower lobe involvement. During the hospitalization, he developed hyponatremia due to SIADH, likely exacerbated by hypothyroidism (TSH ~20), leading to fluid restriction and increased levothyroxine. He had recurrent fevers attributed to aspiration, confirmed by a video swallow study showing aspiration of thin liquids; he was placed on a nectar-thick diet. Abdominal pain was linked to severe constipation and a gastric ulcer with pyloric deformity found on EGD. Electrolyte abnormalities consistent with refeeding syndrome were managed with supplementation. A PICC line was placed for reliable access. He remained in normal sinus rhythm, and diltiazem was held due to low blood pressure. He improved clinically, was stabilized, and discharged home with services and multiple follow-up appointments.
problems: Syndrome of inappropriate secretion of antidiuretic hormone
Gastric ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without hemorrhage or perforation
Other disorders of electrolyte and fluid balance, not elsewhere classified
Pneumonitis due to inhalation of food and vomit
